agree.reason: Starting with her own $600K figure and showing that a 13% cut covers the cost gives Dana a concrete reason to take a 20-minute call, though she may still be wary of her IT director.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief and the halving is tied to one named customer rather than claimed broadly, but leaving out the weaker 2.8-to-2.2 result lets the best case pass as typical.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the $75,000 annual cost for five sites and the roughly 13% break-even against $600K, both correct and favourable, but it never states the stronger point that a halving like the pet distributor's would be worth about $300K a year.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is implied as the $600K-a-year loss continuing, which is accurate, but the email never says outright that this cost recurs every year.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is "see whether those numbers hold up," which names nothing Dana can check, such as an error-rate target or a trial date, even though the evidence comes from a single customer.

objections.reason: "Sits on top of it" and "three weeks" deal with the fear of replacing the warehouse system, but the email never says how little IT work or system integration is needed, which is what the resistant IT director will ask about.

fit.reason: It is short, broken into phone-sized paragraphs, has a specific subject line and ends with one clear ask, as the brief requested.
